questions.stem: The displacement of a plane progressive wave in a medium, travelling towards positive x-axis with velocity 4m/s at t = 0 is given by $y = 3\sin 2\pi\left(-\frac{x}{3}\right)$. Then the expression for the displacement at a later time t = 4 sec will be
questions.solution:
Let $y = 3\sin[\omega t - kx]$
at $t = 0$, $y = 3\sin(-kx)$
$k = \frac{2\pi}{3}$
$v = \frac{\omega}{k}$
$4 = \frac{\omega}{2\pi/3} \Rightarrow \omega = \frac{8\pi}{3}$
$\therefore y = 3\sin\left[\frac{8\pi}{3}t - \frac{2\pi}{3}x\right]$
$\therefore t = 4$
$y = 3\sin\left[\frac{8\pi}{3} \times 4 - \frac{2\pi}{3}x\right]$
$= 3\sin 2\pi\left[\frac{-x + 16}{3}\right]$
$y = 3\sin\left[2\pi\left(-\frac{x - 16}{3}\right)\right]$

questions.stem: Six molecules of an ideal gas have velocities 1, 3, 5, 5, 6 and 5 m/s respectively. At any given temperature, if $\overline{V}$ and $V_{rms}$ represent average and rms speed of the molecules, then

$\overline{V}_{rms} = \sqrt{\frac{1 + 9 + 25 \times 3 + 36}{6}} = \sqrt{\frac{121}{6}} = \frac{11}{\sqrt{6}} = 4.48$

questions.stem: As shown in the figure, a pump is designed as horizontal cylinder with a piston having area A and an outlet orifice having an area ‘a’. The piston moves with a constant velocity under the action of force F. If the density of the liquid is $\rho$, then the speed of the liquid emerging from the orifice is, (assume $A >> a$)
questions.solution:
by principle of continuity
$AV = av$
by Bernoulis principle
$P + \frac{1}{2}\rho V^{2} = P_0 + \frac{1}{2}\rho v^{2}$
$\left[\frac{F}{A} + P_0\right] + \frac{1}{2}\rho V^{2} = P_0 + \frac{1}{2}\rho v^{2}$
$\frac{F}{A} + \frac{1}{2}\rho\left[\frac{av}{A}\right]^{2} = \frac{1}{2}\rho v^{2}$
$\frac{F}{A} = \frac{1}{2}\rho v^{2}\left[1 - \frac{a^{2}}{A^{2}}\right]$
$v = \sqrt{\frac{2F}{\rho A\left[1 - \frac{a^{2}}{A^{2}}\right]}}$
$a^{2} << A^{2}$
$v = \sqrt{\frac{2F}{\rho A}}$

questions.stem: Two substance A and B of same mass are heated at constant rate. The variation of temperature $\theta$ of the substance with time t is shown in the figure. Choose the correct staement
questions.solution:
$\Delta H = mC\Delta\theta$
$\frac{dH}{dt} = mC\frac{d\theta}{dt}$, $\frac{dH}{dt}$ = a constant
$\therefore \frac{d\theta}{dt} \propto \frac{1}{C}$
i.e. slope $\propto \frac{1}{C}$, $\therefore C_B < C_A$

options.text: Specific heat of A is greater than that of B
Specific heat of B is greater than that of A
None of the above is true

questions.stem: An interference pattern is obtained with two coherent sources of intensity ratio n : 1. The ratio $\frac{I_{Max} - I_{Min}}{I_{Max} + I_{Min}}$ will be maximum if
questions.solution:
$\frac{I_1}{I_2} = n$
$I_1 = nI_2$
$I_{max} = \left(\sqrt{I_1} + \sqrt{I_2}\right)^{2} = \left(\sqrt{nI_2} + \sqrt{I_2}\right)^{2} = \left(\sqrt{n} + 1\right)^{2}\left(\sqrt{I_2}\right)^{2}$
$I_{min} = \left(\sqrt{I_1} - \sqrt{I_2}\right)^{2} = \left(\sqrt{nI_2} - \sqrt{I_2}\right)^{2} = \left(\sqrt{n} - 1\right)^{2}\left(\sqrt{I_2}\right)^{2}$
$\frac{I_{max} - I_{min}}{I_{max} + I_{min}} = \frac{\left(\sqrt{n} + 1\right)^{2}(I_2) - \left(\sqrt{n} - 1\right)^{2}I_2}{\left(\sqrt{n} + 1\right)^{2}I_2 + \left(\sqrt{n} - 1\right)^{2}I_2} = \frac{\left(\sqrt{n} + 1\right)^{2} - \left(\sqrt{n} - 1\right)^{2}}{\left(\sqrt{n} + 1\right)^{2} + \left(\sqrt{n} - 1\right)^{2}}$
$= \frac{\left(n + 1 + 2\sqrt{n}\right) - \left(n + 1 - 2\sqrt{n}\right)}{n + 1 + 2\sqrt{n} + n + 1 - 2\sqrt{n}} = \frac{4\sqrt{n}}{2(n + 1)} = \frac{2\sqrt{n}}{n + 1}$
$\therefore$ decreases with increasing n.
$\therefore$ It will be maximum if n = 1

questions.stem: Three identical convex lenses each of focal length f are placed in a straight line separated by a distance f from each other. An object is located at $f/2$ in front of the leftmost lens. Then,
questions.solution:
For first lens
$u = -\frac{f}{2}$
$\frac{1}{f} = \frac{1}{v} - \frac{1}{u} \Rightarrow \frac{1}{f} = \frac{1}{v} - \frac{1}{\frac{-f}{2}} \Rightarrow \frac{1}{v} = \frac{1}{f} - \frac{2}{f} \Rightarrow \frac{1}{v} = \frac{-1}{f}$
$v = -f$
$m_1 = \frac{v}{u} = \frac{-f}{\frac{-f}{2}} = 2$
For second lens
$u = -(f + f) = -2f$
$\frac{1}{v} - \frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{f} \Rightarrow \frac{1}{v} - \frac{1}{-2f} = \frac{1}{f} \Rightarrow \frac{1}{v} = \frac{1}{f} - \frac{1}{2f} \Rightarrow \frac{1}{v} = \frac{1}{2f}$
$v = 2f$
$m_1 = \frac{v}{u} = \frac{2f}{-2f} = -1$
For third lens
$u = f$
$f = f$
$\frac{1}{v} - \frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{f} \Rightarrow \frac{1}{v} = \frac{1}{f} + \frac{1}{u} \Rightarrow \frac{1}{v} = \frac{1}{f} + \frac{1}{f} \Rightarrow \frac{1}{v} = \frac{2}{f} \Rightarrow v = \frac{f}{2}$
$m_3 = \frac{v}{u} = \frac{\frac{f}{2}}{f} = \frac{1}{2}$
Total magnification = $m_1 m_2 m_3 = 2 \times (-1) \times \frac{1}{2} = -1$

options.text: Final image will be at $f/2$ behind the rightmost lens and its magnification will be $-1$.
Final image will be at $f/2$ behind the rightmost lens and its magnification will be $+1$.
Final image will be at f behind the rightmost lens and its magnification will be $-1$.
Final image will be at f behind the rightmost lens and its magnification will be $+1$.

questions.stem: A particle of mass m is projected at a velocity u, making an angle $\theta$ with the horizontal (x – axis). If the angle of projection $\theta$ is varied keeping all other parameters same, then magnitude of angular momentum (L) at its maximum height about the point of projection varies with $\theta$ as,
questions.solution:
$L_0 = mu\cos\theta\,H$
$= mu\cos\theta\frac{u^{2}\sin^{2}\theta}{2g}$
$= \frac{mu^{3}\sin^{2}\theta\cos\theta}{2g}$
L is zero for $\theta = 0^\circ$ and $\theta = \frac{\pi}{2}$

questions.solution:
F = ma
$= m\sqrt{a_c^{2} + a_T^{2}}$
$= m\sqrt{\left(\frac{20}{5}\right)^{2} + 9}$
$= 2\sqrt{16 + 9} = 2 \times 5 = 10$N

questions.stem: A mouse of mass m jumps on the outside edge of a rotating ceiling fan of moment of inertia I and radius R. The fractional loss of angular velocity of the fan as a result is
questions.solution:
$I\omega_0 = \left(I + mR^{2}\right)\omega$, $\omega_0 \to$ Initial angular velocity
$\omega = \frac{I\omega_0}{I + mR^{2}}$, $\omega \to$ Final angular velocity
So, $\frac{\omega_0 - \omega}{\omega_0} = I - \frac{I}{I + mR^{2}} = \frac{mR^{2}}{I + mR^{2}}$

questions.stem: There are n elastic balls placed on a smooth horizontal plane. The masses of the balls are $m, \frac{m}{2}, \frac{m}{2^{2}}, \ldots \frac{m}{2^{n-1}}$ respectively. If the first ball hits the second ball with velocity $v_0$, then the velocity of the $n^{th}$ ball will be,
questions.solution:
1st Collision
$V_1 = \frac{2 \times m}{\frac{m}{2} + m}V_0 = \frac{4}{3}V_0$
2nd Collision
$V_2 = \frac{2 \times \frac{m}{2}}{\frac{m}{2} + \frac{m}{2^{2}}} \times V_0 = \left(\frac{4}{3}\right)^{2}V_0$
3rd Collision
$\left(\frac{4}{3}\right)^{3}V_0$
. . . . .(n – 1) collision, $\therefore V_{n-1} = \left(\frac{4}{3}\right)^{n-1}V_0$

$\Rightarrow T \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{\rho}}$
If T are equal, so will be $\rho$

questions.stem: A bar magnet falls from rest under gravity through the centre of a horizontal ring of conducting wire as shown in figure. Which of the following graph best represents the speed (v) vs. time (t) graph of the bar magnet?
An amount of charge Q passes through a coil of resistance R. If the current in the coil decreases to zero at a uniform rate during time T, then the amount of heat generated in the coil will be,
questions.solution:
Given, $\frac{1}{2}I_0T = Q \Rightarrow I_0 = \frac{2Q}{T}$
Equation of $I(t) \Rightarrow \frac{I}{I_0} + \frac{t}{T} = 1$
$I = I_0\left(1 - \frac{t}{T}\right) = \frac{2Q}{T}\left(1 - \frac{t}{T}\right)$
Heat = $\int_{0}^{T} I^{2}R\,df$
$= R\int_{0}^{T}\frac{4Q^{2}}{T^{2}}\left(1 - \frac{t}{T}\right)^{2}$
$= \frac{4Q^{2}R}{T^{2}}\left[\int_{0}^{T}dt + \frac{1}{T^{2}}\int_{0}^{T}t^{2}dt - \frac{2}{T}\int_{0}^{T}t\,dt\right] = \frac{4Q^{2}R}{T^{2}}\left[\cancel{T} + \frac{T}{3} - \cancel{T}\right] = \frac{4Q^{2}R}{3T}$

questions.stem: A modified gravitational potential is given by $V = -\frac{GM}{r} + \frac{A}{r^{2}}$. If the constant A is expressed in terms of gravitational constant (G), mass (M) and velocity of light (c), then from dimensional analysis, A is,
questions.solution:
$V = -\frac{GM}{r} + \frac{A}{r^{2}}$
$[A] = \frac{[GM]}{[r]}[r^{2}] = [GM][r]$
now, we know, $\frac{GM}{r}$ gives dimension of $c^{2}$
$\frac{[GM]}{[r]} = [c^{2}] \Rightarrow [r] = \frac{[GM]}{[c^{2}]}$
$\Rightarrow [A] = \frac{[GM][GM]}{[c^{2}]}$
$[A] = \frac{G^{2}M^{2}}{c^{2}}$

questions.stem: The figure shows two identical parallel plate capacitors A and B of capacitances C connected to a battery. The key K is initially closed. The switch is now opened and the free spaces between the plates of the capacitors are filled with a dielectric constant 3. Then which of the following statement (s) is/are true?
questions.solution:
$U = \frac{1}{2} \times 2CV^{2}$
$= CV^{2}$
$U_A = \frac{1}{2}(KC)V^{2} = \frac{3}{2}CV^{2}$
$U_B = \frac{q^{2}}{2KC} = \frac{[CV]^{2}}{2KC} = \frac{CV^{2}}{2K} = \frac{1}{6}CV^{2}$
Total energy when switch is open
$U = \frac{1}{2}KCV^{2} + \frac{1}{6}CV^{2}$
$= \frac{3}{2}CV^{2} + \frac{1}{6}CV^{2}$
$= \frac{10}{6}CV^{2} = \frac{5}{3}CV^{2}$

options.text: Which the switch is closed, total energy stored in the two capacitors is $CV^{2}$
When the switch is opened, no charge is stored in the capacitor B
When the switch is opened, energy stored in the capacitor B is $\frac{3}{2}CV^{2}$
When the switch is opened, total energy stored in two capacitors is $\frac{5}{2}CV^{2}$

questions.stem: A charged particle of charge q and mass m is placed at a distance 2R from the centre of a vertical cylindrical region of radius R where magnetic field varies as $\vec{B} = \left(4t^{2} - 2t + 6\right)\hat{k}$ where t is time. Then which of the following statement(s) is/are true?
questions.solution:
$r < R$
$E \times 2\pi r = \frac{d\phi}{dt} = \frac{d}{dt}\left(4t^{2} - 2t + 6\right) \times \pi r^{2}$
$E \times 2\pi r = (8t - 2)\pi r^{2}$
$E = \frac{(8t - 2)r}{2}$
$E = (4t - 1)r$
$E \propto r$
For $r > R$
$E \times 2\pi.(2R) = \frac{d}{dt}[4t^{2} - 2t + 6] \times \pi[R]^{2}$
$E.4\pi R = [8t - 2]\pi R^{2}$
$E = \frac{[8t - 2]R}{4}$ at t = 2, $E = \frac{14}{4}R = \frac{7R}{2}$
acceleration = $\frac{Eq}{m} = \frac{7Rq}{2m} = \frac{7qR}{2m}$

options.text: Induced electric field lines form closed loops
Electric field varies linearly with r if $r < R$, where r is the radial distance from the centerline of the cylinder
The charged particle will move in clockwise direction when viewed from top
Acceleration of the charged particle is $\frac{7q}{2m}$ when t = 2 sec

questions.stem: A uniform magnetic field B exists in a region. An electron of charge q and mass m moving with velocity v enters the region in a direction perpendicular to the magnetic field. Considering Bohr angular momentum quantization, which of the following statement(s) is/are true?
questions.solution:
$r = \frac{mv}{qB}$
$mvr = \frac{nh}{2\pi}$
$mv = \frac{nh}{2\pi r}$
$r = \frac{nh}{2\pi rqB}$
$r^{2} = \frac{nh}{2\pi qB} \Rightarrow r = \sqrt{\frac{nh}{2\pi qB}}$
$r \propto \sqrt{n}$
$v = \frac{qBr}{m} = \frac{qB}{m}\sqrt{\frac{nh}{2\pi qB}}$
$v_{min} = \sqrt{\frac{q^{2}B^{2}}{m^{2}} \times \frac{nh}{2\pi qB}} = \sqrt{\frac{nqBh}{2\pi m^{2}}} = \frac{1}{m}\sqrt{qB\hbar}$
$E = \frac{1}{2}mv^{2}$
$= \frac{1}{2}m\left[\frac{nqBh}{2\pi m^{2}}\right]$
$E \propto n$
$E_2 - E_1 = (n_2 - n_1)\frac{qBh}{4\pi m}$
$hf = (n_2 - n_1)\frac{qBh}{4\pi m}$
$n_2 - n_1 = 1$ for successive levels

options.text: The maximum velocity of the electron is $\frac{\sqrt{qB\hbar}}{m}$
Transition frequency $\omega$ between two successive levels is independent of n

questions.stem: A train is moving along the tracks at a constant speed u. A girl on the train throws a ball of mass m straight ahead along the direction of motion of the train with speed v with respect to herself. Then
questions.solution:
w.r.t. the girl $E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv^{2}$
$\therefore W = \Delta E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv^{2}$
Work by the train = $\left\{\frac{1}{2}(v + u)^{2} - \frac{1}{2}mu^{2}\right\} - \frac{1}{2}mv^{2}$
$= \frac{1}{2}m\left(v^{2} + u^{2} + 2vu\right) - \frac{1}{2}m\left(v^{2} + u^{2}\right)$
$= mvu$
Gain in $E_k$ = $\frac{1}{2}m(v + u)^{2} - \frac{1}{2}mu^{2} = \frac{1}{2}mv^{2} + mvu$
measured from rail track

options.text: Kinetic energy of the ball as measured by the girl on the train is $mv^{2}/2$
Work done by the girl in throwing the ball is $mv^{2}/2$
Work done by the train is $mvu$
The gain in kinetic energy of the ball as measured by a person standing by the rail track is $mv^{2}/2$
